parts.name: arm strip 0

physics.Basic_description: A long, slender wooden strip with a smooth brown finish, forming the lower arm of the tongs.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the stationary jaw of the tongs, providing a surface against which the moving arm presses to grip objects.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can grasp this arm near the handle end to stabilize the tool while operating the other arm.
physics.reason: Wooden tongs arms are typically solid slats of wood bent into shape, not hollow shells.

parts.name: wood bend

physics.Basic_description: The curved U-shaped section at the rear where the two wooden strips join, showing continuous wood grain.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the spring-like elasticity that allows the tongs to open and close without a separate metal hinge.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and structurally critical to grasp directly; gripping here might damage the bend or provide poor leverage.
physics.reason: This is the bent portion of the solid wood slat, maintaining the same cross-section as the arms.

parts.name: arm strip 1

physics.Basic_description: The upper wooden strip, matching the lower one in material and finish, featuring a slightly bulbous tip for gripping.
physics.Functional_description: The active jaw that flexes towards the fixed arm when squeezed, creating the clamping force.
physics.Grasped_description: The primary actuation point; a gripper would press down on the mid-section or handle of this arm to close the tongs.
physics.reason: Like the fixed arm, this is a solid piece of wood shaped into a strip.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
